title: The only habit tracker that actually changed my behavior
body:
I’ve tried many habit trackers over the years, but Awesome Habits is the first one that genuinely became part of my life.

What I love most is how simple and frictionless it feels. There is no unnecessary complexity, no gamification overload, no feeling that managing the habit tracker becomes a habit in itself. You open the app, see exactly what matters, complete your habits, and move on with your day.

Over time, that simplicity had a much bigger effect on me than I expected. Awesome Habits helped me turn things I wanted to do occasionally into things I now do consistently. Health, supplementation, training, routines and other small daily behaviors became much easier to maintain because I could actually see my consistency accumulating over months.

The statistics are also extremely motivating. Seeing long streaks, completion history and hundreds of completed repetitions creates a real sense of continuity. You stop thinking about habits as isolated actions and start seeing them as part of your identity and long-term system.

The design deserves a mention too. It is clean, beautiful and incredibly pleasant to use. It feels like an app designed by people who understand that the best productivity software should reduce friction rather than create more of it.

I recently sent the team a small product suggestion and was genuinely surprised to receive a thoughtful personal response from the developer, who actually understood the idea and added it to their list for future updates. That level of care is rare.

Awesome Habits may look like a simple habit tracker, but for me it has had a surprisingly meaningful impact on how I organize my life and maintain consistency.

One of the very few apps on my phone that I would immediately reinstall on a new device.
author: Simon Miotk

title: I love it!
body:
Integration with apple shortcuts is a huge plus. It allows you to automatize a lot of shortcuts’ actions directly depending on which habits you have or haven’t completed yet. It especially powerful with apple watch and it’s double tap/double clench (etc) gestures.

I think it would be cool if the app had some sort of mechanism, that finds correlations between different habits (correlations that you might normally miss) and inform the user about it. For example: It could inform you when it detects that when you fail “don’t eat late” habit the previous day you usually also fail next day “Morning Run” habit.
author: Dingovv

title: Super!
body: Najlepsza aplikacja do zapisywania nawyków! Zero rozpraszaczy, jak w innych aplikacjach, typu statystyki, wykresy i inne głupoty, które są niepotrzebne i rozpraszają. Dodajcie obsługę Apple Watch i w widżecie możliwość zmiany sposobu wyświetlania zapisanych nawyków w postaci pisemnej, a nie jak jest to do tej pory tylko w formie obrazków. A i proszę nie zmieniajcie nic poza tym! Po krótkim używania aplikacja ma kilka błędów. Kiedy mamy ustawiony np. Weekend wolny od zadań, to w poniedziałek nie zaczytują się nowe nawyki, trzeba edytować jakiś nawyk i wtedy się wczytują. Nie działa połączenie z Apple health.

title: Simple yet powerful habits tracking app
body:
Simple, beautiful and lightweight. It has everything you need to track your habits. It doesn’t distract, just let you focus on your goals. This apps feels and looks just like I imagined the habit tracking app. Great UX/UI!

The only thing I miss is the ability to set habit as a yes/no or done/not done habit. The “count” is still working well for this case of course.

title: Minimalist, functional, powerful!
body:
I've tested a ton of habit and time tracking apps, but this one is hands down the best!

Few people mention it, but it is not only a great application for tracking quantity-based habits, but also an extremely functional time tracker. It works perfectly with Apple Watch and is ideal for the owner of this watch who values simplicity and convenience. For any slightly more advanced users, the supported Siri shortcuts will certainly be useful.

If I had to complain about anything, it would be that the shortcuts do not run in the background but open applications every time you use them. However, I already sent a message about it and the developer said that they plan to improve it.

And did I mention that instead of paying a monthly subscription, you can make a one-time payment?

For anyone who, in addition to tracking their habits, would like to measure time using a watch, this application is a 100% must-have!
